Changing ZRAM size or compression algorithm affects how the system handles memory pressure system-wide. An unsupported combination can cause instability or slow app switching — apply one change at a time and give it a few minutes.
ZRAM resize briefly disables swap while it resets the device, which is normal and only takes a moment. Very large sizes trade some CPU time (for compression) for more usable memory.

FAS (Frame-Aware Scheduling) is a userspace implementation, offering greater versatility and adaptability compared to kernel-level MI FEAS. It monitors frame rendering and dynamically schedules performance to ensure rendering efficiency while minimizing system overhead.

FPSGO (Frames Per Second Go) is a MediaTek kernel module that dynamically adjusts CPU/GPU frequency based on real-time frame rate. It actively lowers frequency to save power when frame rate is stable, and quickly boosts frequency to ensure smoothness when frame rate is strained.
This option is only supported on MediaTek devices
